job.text: Look up each applicant's credit score

source.shows: a categorical dot plot on a scale from the theoretical minimum, 300–500 by 50 (R2-26, G1.57): dots do not encode length, so the scale need not reach zero; hollow dots, the plain style's for categorical dot plots, and “500 (credit score)” on the top label, as the book draws it

reasons.chart.value_labels: the bad version's point is its scale from zero (p. 89), which value labels would take away

source.shows: the same spec as bars: bars start at zero, never at the theoretical minimum, so the scale shows scores no one can have, and the differences shrink; the procedure gives dots (G1.57, D-30), a guided finding
